messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Dedicated pool dp-eu-central-3 reporting sustained GPU saturation for tenant nova-analytics. Avg GPU utilization 97%. Severity: P1. Thread created 3100007777
oncall-sre: ack. grabbing high-priority channel. Priya, can you pull pool topology and active allocations?
oliver: pulling now. Preliminary: pool has 12 GPUs, nova-analytics currently holds 10 pinned GPUs across 5 hosts. Other tenants unaffected (<=30% util).
priya: impact from CS: some Nova dashboards timing out and batch ingest jobs failing with OOM on worker-shard. Reported since ~10:04 CET.
devin: are autoscaler actions failing? any pending requests for additional nodes?
infra-bot: autoscaler event: scale-request-31101 created at 3100007802 -> status: rejected by cloud due to AZ capacity constraint. Retry count 2.
oliver: cloud region eu-central has low spare NVIDIA inventory this morning; our request is queued behind marketplace demand.
amanda: what's contract for Nova? Any emergency burst clause?
priya: Nova is Enterprise dedicated with a 'burst-on-approval' clause but not enabled by default. AM informed and reachable.
oncall-sre: mitigation ideas (ranked): 1) apply short-term rate-limits and fair-share across Nova's endpoints, 2) enable emergency shared-burst (if AM approves) to attach +3 GPUs, 3) force config switch to small-int8 model for interactive endpoints, 4) offload long-running batch to cold nodes (queue and retry).
devin: we should avoid full migration between pools (too risky). Fair-share + model swap seems fastest.
oliver: implementing fair-share: `routerctl set-qos --tenant nova-analytics --policy fair-share --weights realtime:70,batch:30 --max-concurrency 250`
priya: setting model override for realtime endpoints to rdlm-int8-lite. Command: `routerctl override-model --tenant nova-analytics --route /v1/chat --model rdlm-int8-lite --duration 90m`
oncall-sre: note: rdlm-int8-lite reduces vram usage ~2.5x, expect slight quality/latency tradeoffs. Notify AM/CS.
amanda: I've messaged Nova AM; they asked for two options: safe temporary throttling + model switch, or enable burst and accept pass-through billing. They prefer we try throttling+model first, but want burst as fallback.
infra-bot: throttling changes applied at 3100007865. Previous inflight queue 380 -> now 160.
oliver: quick health snapshot after actions:
```
pool dp-eu-central-3: 12 GPUs total
pre-change per-GPU util: [95,98,99,96,97,99,94,98,99,98,93,95]
post-change per-GPU util (sample): [68,70,66,72,69,71,65,67,70,68,63,64]
avg latency interactive: 0.9s (was 2.8s)
batch failures: decreased but some backlog remains (~120 jobs)
```
devin: batch backlog: recommend moving low-priority batch jobs to deferred queue with exponential backoff: `batchctl requeue --tenant nova-analytics --priority <= low --delay 15m`
priya: doing that now. Also enabling alert routing to oncall-sre for any relapses for next 2 hours.
oncall-sre: AM approved burst if needed. I'll file cloud burst: `cloudctl emergency-attach --region eu-central-3 --gpucount 3 --tags emergency:nova` request submitted id cloud-req-31102.
infra-bot: cloud request queued at position 5 (estimate ~20-40m).
amanda: Nova engineering wants a short customer-facing statement now. Draft: "We're experiencing elevated GPU usage in your dedicated pool causing slower responses and some batch failures. We've applied rate-limits and switched interactive endpoints to a lightweight model; we expect performance to improve shortly. If needed, we'll attach temporary capacity and share cost details. We will follow up with a full incident note." Approve?
oliver: approve. Add ETA: 30-60m to full recovery depending on cloud queue.
priya: metrics show progressive improvement. Queue length dropping. Watchlist: memory pressure on host h-7 where two processes show repeated OOM kills.
devin: isolating problematic worker on h-7: `infractl isolate-host --host h-7 --drain --timeout 5m` then restart model-server process with memory guard.
oliver: host drained and model-server restarted. No further OOMs observed after 2 restarts.
oncall-sre: cloud attached +3 GPUs at 3100008389 (burst success). After attachment, utilization normalized further.
infra-bot: post-attach per-GPU util: [55,58,53,60,57,59,52,54,56,55,50,51, 38,40,42] (last three are burst GPUs).
priya: CS confirms dashboards responsive again and batch requeues being processed. Nova AM requested a bridge for postmortem; scheduled for tomorrow 13:00 CET.
amanda: logging the incident: INC-2026-908, tagging nova-analytics and eng-runtime.
oncall-sre: follow-ups to assign: 1) ensure pre-approved emergency-burst flags are added to Enterprise contracts, 2) add automated fallback policy to enable model override for designated tenants when GPU util >90% for >5min, 3) increase regional reserved capacity in eu-central-3 from 8->12 GPUs.
oliver: creating epic in tracker and assigning owners. Also will attach config diffs and metric slices to the incident ticket. `git diff configs/pools/dp-eu-central-3 > /tmp/dp-eu-central-3-diff.txt`
devin: handing off monitoring to Priya for the next 60 minutes. I'll stay on call for infra escalations.
priya: handoff ack. Will post updates every 10m or on state change.
oncall-sre: status -> mitigated (recovered) but incident remains open for follow-up actions. Closing the emergency page. :white_check_mark:
